thread:
sara: Heads-up — customer T-945 reporting truncated JSON in streaming responses. About 10-15% of their /v1/streams calls end mid-object. Customer payload tail:
```json
{"id":"resp_123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Thanks for your...\"}} // <-- stream cuts here
```
Parse error thrown on client: Unexpected end of JSON input. They say it started after we enabled the edge TCP optimizations last week.

matt: Can you paste a request_id and region? Any proxy in front of the client (CF, nginx)?

sara: req ids: 01FJ4A2X9H, 01FJ4A2Y3K, region us-west-2. Customer path: client -> Cloudflare -> our LB -> edge -> runtime. They attached a minimal curl that reproduces for them (~20 attempts yields a cutoff in ~2):
```bash
# reproducer (customer)
TOKEN=REDACTED
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-x","input":"stream json mode test","mode":"json_stream"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
Notes: they use HTTP/1.1; if they try HTTP/2 it seems less frequent.

alex: "-N" is fine. Could be a chunk boundary issue where upstream closes TCP mid-chunk (staccato fragmentation). Can we get edge traces for those req ids and the TCP close reason? Also check keepalive settings between CF->LB and LB->edge.

ingress-bot: edge-deploy: v3.2.1 rolled 3759998800, no crashloop alerts. Observability: small bump in FIN from connections: +0.8% in last 24h.

mike: I'm thinking proxy buffering + early FIN on idle keepalive. Two quick tests: 1) client -> direct to our LB (bypass CF) to confirm CF involvement; 2) curl with http2: `curl --http2 -N ...` to see if problem disappears (h2 multiplexing changes framing). Also try `--no-buffer` and capture raw bytes (nc) to see chunk boundaries.

sara: Customer tried bypassing CF -> still saw 6% failures (lower but still present). They captured raw tail showing last bytes before EOF: `...\"content\":\"...done\"}}\r\n` then immediate EOF (no closing ]}). Edge raw log shows: `upstream_status=FIN, bytes_sent=1456, write_timeout=0` for one sample.

matt: That indicates the upstream side (runtime) closed the connection without emitting final frames. Can eng-runtime reproduce locally with a high token-rate prompt? @alex can you run a run-local with an artificially small socket send window to simulate fragmentation?

alex: On it. I'll run a stress job with TCP window=256B and a model that emits many small delta chunks. If I can repro, next step is to capture the sequence numbers and kernel socket state to see if the runtime call path ever returns early.

mike: If runtime returns early we need to check for exceptions in the generation loop or KV cache flush code. Also confirm we aren't hitting our internal max-response-size gating and closing the stream as part of a safety path (would be obvious in logs).

sara: Customer asked for workaround; I suggested switching to non-streaming JSON or adding client-side reassembly/retry logic for truncated streams. They prefer streaming.

matt: Please attach trace links and logs to the ticket. If alex can repro, escalate to eng-runtime with captured pcap and chunk boundary dump (hex). @alex @mike can you prioritize?

alex: Will post repro artifacts here by 3759998960. Preliminary: I can reproduce ~repeatable when small socket write bursts + keepalive probe races — calls drop after a short FIN sent from runtime process.

mike: Good find. Plan: 1) instrument runtime to log final emit/close reason (graceful vs forced), 2) add a short delay to ensure final buffer flush before close (temp mitigation), 3) investigate kernel-level RST vs FIN cause.

sara: Thanks. I'll update customer with actionable repro and ask them to test http2 path as a short-term mitigation. Will add customer logs to the escalations ticket. :thumbsup:

ingress-bot: ticket T-945 updated: escalated -> eng-runtime, priority P2.
